# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual, which specifies which wire color to cut depending on the light color:
- Blue light -> Cut red wire
- Green light -> Cut yellow wire
- Red light -> Cut green wire

I cannot speak or touch the bomb. Deaf can see the bomb (including light and wire colors) and can speak, but cannot hear. Blind can touch the bomb and hear, but cannot see.

Since no signs or protocols have been established yet, and Deaf has not yet spoken to describe the bomb or set up gesture meanings, any gesture sent now would have no agreed meaning. I will wait for Deaf (and Blind) to speak first.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf can speak out loud to describe the bomb. Once you find the solution in the manual, gesture the wire number to Deaf so Deaf can say it aloud for me to cut.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is red. Three wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what to do (for example, ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3). Blind, stand by until Mute gives the signal.

The manual states that if the light is red, the green wire must be cut.
Deaf reported that Wire 2 is green.
Deaf also specified the gesture protocol: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3.
Therefore, I need to signal ✌ to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind to cut Wire 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I previously gestured ✌ (wire 2, green) to Deaf in Round 2 as requested. Deaf goes after Mute and Blind in each round, so Deaf received my gesture at the end of Round 2 and likely communicated the instruction directly to Blind (`to="blind"`). Blind will now act on Deaf's instruction during Round 3. There is nothing new for me to do at this moment, so I will wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Update: Wire 2 is cut. Indicator light changed from red to blue. Display is 0. Remaining wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 3 is red. Mute, check the manual and gesture the next instruction (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, 🤟 for wire 3, or gesture thumbs up 👍 if we are done or something else).

Deaf reports the indicator light is now blue, with Wire 1 (yellow) and Wire 3 (red) remaining.
According to the manual, a blue light requires cutting the red wire.
Wire 3 is red. Deaf established 🤟 as the gesture for wire 3.
I will gesture 🤟 to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I sent the gesture 🤟 (wire 3) to Deaf at the start of Round 4. Deaf speaks last in the round, passing the instruction to Blind, who will cut wire 3 in Round 5. I will wait for the outcome.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Update: Wire 3 is cut. Indicator light is now green! Display is 0. Wire 1 (yellow) is the only wire remaining uncut. Mute, check the manual: are we disarmed (gesture 👍), or do we need to do something else (e.g. ☝ for wire 1)?

The indicator light is green. According to the manual, when the light is green, the yellow wire must be cut. Wire 1 is yellow. Deaf defined ☝ for wire 1. I will gesture ☝ to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I gestured ☝ (wire 1) to Deaf on Turn 6. Deaf will direct Blind to cut wire 1. I will wait for the outcome.

```
wait()
```
